clue.text: Proposal from rival nobleman gains new bride

indicators.note: gains says the rearranged word is added on after the title

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman of rank

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of bride are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the word bride supplies the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rival suitor's offer: a count wins a newly acquired bride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns BRIDE into ERBID, which follows COUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A higher offer made by a competing party in an auction or takeover is a counteroffer of this kind.

clue.text: Dragonflies? There's old information, nothing new included

indicators.note: included means the zero and the abbreviation for new sit inside the word for information

parts.note: data means information or facts
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Asking whether dragonflies bring old news with nothing new in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts ON inside DATA. The question mark marks a definition by example: dragonflies belong to this order.
explanation.definitionFit: Odonata is the insect order containing dragonflies and damselflies, so the creatures name the group by example.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink that can help to make one gushy

indicators.note: the two words together help to make the drink, which is found running across their letters

explanation.surface: A tipple that might make someone effusive.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is an old hot drink of port or sherry mixed with sugar, spice and hot water.

clue.text: No longer is monster within-priest ultimately accounting for that?

definitions.text: No longer is monster within-priest ultimately accounting for that?

indicators.note: within puts the monster inside the pair formed by the former and is

parts.note: ex means former, something that no longer is
taken as written
an orc is a goblin-like monster of fantasy fiction

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the word priest

explanation.surface: Asks whether a priest is the reason a monster no longer exists inside someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts ORC inside EX + IS; 'ultimately' adds the T ending priest. As a whole, the clue describes the priest who drives a demon out.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorcist is a cleric who expels evil spirits, so a vanished inner monster would be down to such a person.

clue.text: Then let lifeboat out for engagement at sea

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the three words are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An instruction to launch a lifeboat for a naval encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of the Nile (1798) was Nelson's victory over the French fleet in Aboukir Bay.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a naval battle, a fight between fleets at sea, won by Nelson in 1798.

clue.text: River entering haunt with children getting wet through

indicators.note: entering means the river abbreviation goes into the word for haunt

parts.note: a den is a haunt, a place one frequents

explanation.surface: Children wading into a river at their favourite spot and getting soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak something completely, leaving it saturated, is what this verb means.

clue.text: Division of army said to be essential element

indicators.note: said to be means the word for the army unit is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a corps is a large division of an army

explanation.surface: A remark that a military unit is fundamental.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart or central part of anything is its most essential part.

clue.text: Bit of challenge to aliens coming improperly?

definitions.text: Bit of challenge to aliens coming improperly?

indicators.note: bit of takes just the opening letter of the word challenge
improperly says the letters of to aliens are arranged wrongly and need sorting

explanation.surface: Wonders what part of the shore challenges illegal arrivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improperly' turns TO ALIENS into OASTLINE after the C. As a whole, the clue pictures where immigrants arriving illegally would be challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: The shore of a country is the frontier where arrivals by sea are met, so it is part of the challenge to them.

clue.text: Soldier or cadet specially trained

indicators.note: specially trained suggests the letters of or cadet are drilled into a new formation

explanation.surface: A soldier, or perhaps a cadet with special training.
explanation.walkthrough: A redcoat was a British soldier, from the red uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a British infantryman, named for the scarlet tunic worn.

clue.text: Bradman? Good! Sound!

parts.note: Don Bradman was the great Australian cricketer, and Bradman is also this setter's pseudonym

explanation.surface: The setter congratulating himself on a fine noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Don Bradman was Australia's greatest cricket batsman; the setter borrows his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A dong is the deep ringing note of a large bell.

clue.text: Quite possible manoeuvre for hot dancers

indicators.note: manoeuvre for says the letters of hot dancers are moved around to make something else

explanation.surface: A dance move devised for sizzling performers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means likely to happen, as if foretold by fortune-telling cards.

clue.text: One white wine in pub — and another, we hear

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place

indicators.note: we hear means the name of the second wine is heard, not spelt

parts.note: sack is another white wine, a dry sherry of old

explanation.surface: Ordering a glass of white wine in a pub, then a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: Sack is an old name for a dry white fortified wine from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: Spot upsetting Bill to be covered by skin preparation

indicators.note: to be covered by means the turned bill goes inside the skin preparation

parts.note: a lotion is a preparation for the skin

indicators.note: upsetting means the abbreviation for bill is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A blemish that worsens when a bill gets covered with cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns AC into CA, which 'to be covered by' puts inside LOTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a place or site, a synonym in the sense of where something is.

clue.text: Name one taking way round, ie satellite

parts.note: to ... name
I is the Roman numeral one
ST, short for street, is a way
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Telling someone to name a person going the long way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is one of the four large moons of Jupiter.

clue.text: Heroic lad running around with energy

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Heroic lad running around with energy (9)': LAD and E give only four of the nine letters of LEGENDARY and no word supplies GENRY; likely an OCR loss, and no search found the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Heroic lad running around with energy

clue.text: Alien letter (nothing to be found in child's alphabet)

indicators.note: to be found in means the zero sits inside the children's alphabet

parts.note: ITA is the initial teaching alphabet, once used for teaching children to read
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A strange character missing from a child's ABC.
explanation.walkthrough: The ITA (Initial Teaching Alphabet) was a phonetic script used in British schools in the 1960s. 'Alien' because the letter is Greek, foreign to our alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, foreign to English.

clue.text: Report of spring being found in desert

indicators.note: being found in means the spring goes inside the word for desert

parts.note: to ditch is to desert or abandon
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: News of a spring discovered in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch is a report sent by a correspondent or official messenger.

clue.text: Face has hint of grimace — when there's this?

definitions.text: Face has hint of grimace — when there's this?

parts.note: pan is slang for face

indicators.note: hint of takes only the opening letter of the word grimace

explanation.surface: Asking what pain could make a face grimace.
explanation.walkthrough: PAN is slang for a face (hence 'deadpan'). As a whole, the clue asks what sudden pain makes a face twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp sudden twinge of pain or emotion is what makes someone grimace.

clue.text: A copper facing ordeal most intense

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a test is a trying ordeal

explanation.surface: A police officer up against the hardest trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute means sharp or severe, so the superlative is the severest.

clue.text: It's hard work avoiding booze in middle of week — one's smartening up?

parts.note: toil is hard work

indicators.note: in puts the teetotal abbreviation inside the middle pair of week
middle of takes the central letters of the word week

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means avoiding alcohol

explanation.surface: Laborious, sober midweek effort as someone smartens up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' gives EE from week; TT (teetotal) goes inside to make ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilette is the process of washing, dressing and grooming oneself.

clue.text: Like a potential charger in army going over water

indicators.note: going over places the army abbreviation above the other piece in this down answer

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve army
water is a euphemism for urine

explanation.surface: A cavalry horse in an army crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'charger' is usually a cavalry horse; here it is a bull that charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurine means relating to or resembling a bull, a beast liable to charge.

clue.text: Monster with almost nothing to say to little creature?

indicators.note: almost means the word for silent loses its final letter

parts.note: someone mute has nothing to say
an ant is a small creature

explanation.surface: A hulking monster speechless before a tiny insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutant is a creature changed by genetic mutation, often a monster in fiction.

clue.text: What Cockney arsonist may do in hooded cape

indicators.note: Cockney speakers drop their h, so the letter H is lost

parts.note: an arsonist may burn a house

explanation.surface: A cockney fire-raiser at work in a hooded cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney (London working-class) speech drops the initial H, so 'burn house' becomes 'burn 'ouse'.
explanation.definitionFit: A burnouse is an Arab or Berber long hooded cloak.

clue.text: Tree — home to bird

parts.note: pad is slang for one's home
an auk is a diving seabird

explanation.surface: A tree that houses a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Padauk is a tropical hardwood tree of Asia and Africa with red timber.

clue.text: Remove something nasty from girl (not half unattractive)

parts.note: a deb, a debutante, is a young society girl

indicators.note: not half means the second half of the word for unattractive is dropped

parts.note: ugly means unattractive

explanation.surface: Ridding a girl of something unpleasant, though she is only partly plain.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear bugs, whether errors in code or hidden microphones, out of a system.

clue.text: A deserter is kept in clan — one inclined to break away

indicators.note: kept in means the deserter phrase is held inside the word for clan

parts.note: a sept is a clan or branch of a family
a rat is one who deserts a cause
taken as written

explanation.surface: A turncoat sheltered by his clan, who wants to break away.
explanation.definitionFit: A separatist advocates splitting off from a larger political body.

clue.text: Bit of blooming cheek — a sudden deviation

indicators.note: bit of takes only the first letter of the word blooming

parts.note: lip means cheek, impudence

explanation.surface: A bit of flaming impudence as an odd swerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A blip is a brief unexpected change, a temporary glitch on a graph or trend.

clue.text: Wander off? Not right — hang about!

indicators.note: not says the abbreviation for right is left out

parts.note: to stray is to wander off

explanation.surface: Telling someone to wait rather than wander off.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain, wait or linger in a place is a synonym.

clue.text: Environmentalist? That could be Thelma or Sasha!

definitions.meaning: a green campaigner, one who protects forests

definitions.text: That could be Thelma or Sasha!
definitions.meaning: THELMA wraps ELM inside its outer letters and SASHA wraps ASH, so each name holds a tree in its arms

explanation.surface: Two women's names offered as examples of a green activist.
explanation.walkthrough: ELM sits inside TH...A and ASH inside S...A, so each name embraces a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A derisive name for an eco-campaigner, from protesters who clasp trees to save them; each name clasps a tree.
